thread.title: Why ‘the Digital Age’s Enron’ could be ‘one of the great shorts of all time’ - MarketWatch

author: Shawn Langlois
title: Why ‘the Digital Age’s Enron’ could be ‘one of the great shorts of all time’ - MarketWatch
text:
From privacy concerns to #fakenews controversies and plenty of stuff in between, Facebook’s been getting pounded by an onslaught of nasty headlines going back to the whole Cambridge Analytica fiasco that blew up last year.
But, hey, some good headlines could be in the offing.
Facebook FB, +2.18% on Wednesday is expected to post the most profitable quarter in its history , boosted by monster numbers from Instagram.
Barclays analyst Ross Sandler has a $180 price target on the stock, which is trading just under $150 a share. He says he believes all the negativity is priced into the stock and investors would be wise to consider hopping aboard.
“The best opportunity in large cap internet is to catch a quality name when sentiment is washed out, valuation is depressed and positioning is offsides (as experienced with Alphabet GOOG, +1.59% and Amazon AMZN, +0.95% heading into 2015),” he wrote. “This could be the setup for Facebook right now.”
Our call of the day has a decidedly different take, however.
‘The market is drastically underestimating the peril the company is in.’ Trevor Noren, 13D Research Trevor Noren of 13D Research warns “the fall of Facebook has only begun. The platform is broken and neither human nor machine can fix it.”
Even after the stock has lost about a third of its market cap, “it still may prove one of the great shorts of all time,” Noren wrote in a Medium post . “The platform’s content ecosystem is too poisoned for human or machine moderators to cleanse. Users are fleeing in droves, especially in the company’s most valuable markets. Ad buyers are already shifting dollars to competitors’ platforms.”
He added that governments around the world are stepping up to hinder Facebook’s data-collection capabilities and the company is under investigation by the FTC, Justice Dept., SEC, FBI, and several government agencies in Europe.
Noren also believes that it’s just a matter of time before Facebook’s board removes Sheryl Sandberg and Mark Zuckerberg.
“The market is drastically underestimating the peril the company is in,” he said. “Given the company’s leaders still appear blinded by and irrevocably attached to their business model and ideals, we doubt they can stave off the onslaught coming.”
So what’s the final result?
“The institutionalized failure to see and respond to the platform’s downsides,” Noren warned, “may render Facebook the Digital Age’s Enron — a canonized example of how greed and corruption can fell even the mightiest.”
Facebook shares are leaning lower before the opening bell, with the broader stock market poised to limp into the new week.
The market Futures on the Dow Jones Industrial YMH9, -0.43% , Nasdaq Composite NQH9, -0.51% and S&P 500 ESH9, -0.42% are all in the red. Gold GCH9, +1.51% is holding just at $1,300, and crude oil CLH9, -1.71% is down over 1.5% early.

The quote “The difference is that Harris is the only one who, after I helped her, sent word that I would be indicted if I ‘so much as jaywalked’ while she was D.A. That’s politics for ya” — Former San Francisco Mayor Willie Brown, talking about his affair with Kamala Harris , who launched her bid for the presidency with a rally in her hometown Sunday.
The chart This colorful chart comes from the Visual Capitalist blog and uses data from Global Financial Data to illustrate just how much the stock market has evolved over the past two centuries. “While there are some obvious historical moments to be discovered on the chart,” writes Jeff Desjardin, “perhaps the most important lesson it demonstrates is the unpredictability of the market in general.”
Nowadays, as you can see, the market is more diverse than ever:
“The transition is incredible to look at in retrospect, and makes us wonder what the market will look like 100 years from now,” Desjardin wrote.
The stat 63% — That’s the portion of Americans who say they believe the country is on the “wrong track,” according to a recent NBC News/Wall Street Journal poll. “Times are grim,” Democratic pollster Peter Hart, who conducted the survey, told NBC News . “The shutdown is front and center.”
The economy With the government getting back to business, look for those delayed releases to start trickling in. The big report this week is the January jobs number, but we won’t get that until Friday. The schedule on Monday includes the Chicago Fed National Activity Index at 8:30 a.m. Eastern and the Dallas Fed Survey of Manufacturing Activity two hours later. Also, the FOMC meets this week, but no policy tweaks are expected.
